title: ReviewResult v2 — commit-bound review subject (sole owner: the independent reviewer)
description: Versioned successor to the version-1 reviewResult definition, which lived in review.schema.json until round V1-RESULT-RETIRE retired that file on 2026-08-28; the succession is per the user-adjudicated wave-2 design (2026-07-23) and contract supersession-1. Closed runs and shadow rounds keep their frozen packages as pinned v1 history, which is read from the commits that hold it and on which no migration was ever performed; the promise that the v1 file itself stays frozen for that reading was corrected out of contract v4 §13.1 on 2026-08-28 under HD-63, the same defect class and the same sweep. Delta over v1, and nothing else: (1) root schema_version const '2' — the instance names its own schema, and the loader keys on it explicitly with no cross-version fallback (the W1 pattern); (2) 'package_ref' is gone — the review subject is one committed control plane, bound as subject = { evidence_commit, candidate_ref, base_revision, control_root, repair_round }; git content-addresses every member byte, so there are no per-member digests and no hand-authored member list (the w1-r1 freeze-check-paths defect class is unrepresentable here). A result that carries package_ref, or omits subject, fails this schema's closed root. Five definitions are referenced rather than copied — review_round, instruction_completeness, the per-obligation dispositions, the findings and verify_scope — and since round V1-RESULT-RETIRE (2026-08-28) they are referenced from common.schema.json, where this pack's shared definitions live (one home, N0-A6); they moved there byte-equal, and this file is their only referent. verdict and residual_uncertainty are stated inline because no shared $def for either exists to reference: the constraints came from the version-1 reviewResult's inline ones, and the move to common.schema.json extracted nothing new for them. residual_uncertainty is still that v1 constraint unchanged; verdict is not, since round PROMISE-PATH-VOCAB (2026-09-03) added the VERIFY-only value UNRESOLVED_BLOCKER under HD-70 and, with the root enum now the union of the two rounds, gave the FULL round the explicit narrowing the root used to supply on its own. REVIEWED_NO_BLOCKER still means only 'no blocking discrepancy found within the frozen subjects and review dimensions' (N2-A3).

schema_version.description: The instance names its own schema (W1 precedent, design §3.6). v1 results carry no version field; the loader routes on presence/value and never falls back across versions — a present-but-null or unknown value is a SPEC_GAP, fail closed. Absence still routes to the version-1 kind, and since round V1-RESULT-RETIRE (2026-08-28) no registered schema answers to that kind, so such a result is neither validated nor accepted: contract v4 §13.1 prescribes no validation path for it and leaves which mechanism raises the stop to the implementation.

verdict.description: The UNION of the two rounds' closed control verdicts (contract §5); neither round may return all four, and the narrowing that says which is below — both rounds, since round PROMISE-PATH-VOCAB. Unchanged from v1 until that round, which added UNRESOLVED_BLOCKER as a VERIFY-only value under HD-70: it means a blocking finding stands after the single permitted repair, whether the repair failed to close it or created it, and it exists so that SPEC_GAP goes back to meaning what it says — the specification is defective, and a new WorkSpec and a new START are owed. It names the set the AssuranceCandidate already calls unresolved_finding_ids. A FULL never returns it: a FULL that finds a blocker asks for the repair (CHANGES_REQUIRED), and there is no repair left to ask for once the VERIFY is the round in hand.

per_obligation_disposition.description: Every obligation exactly once (invariant 2). That the set matches the WorkSpec's obligations exactly is enforced by the v2-aware result checker, which is the only place both documents are present.

findings.description: Present only when there are findings; absent means none were raised.

residual_uncertainty.description: Disclosed uncertainty as DATA — REQUIRED, empty array permitted, exactly as in v1: an omitted field cannot be distinguished from 'the reviewer never considered it'.

reviewed_by.description: The independent reviewer that owns this result. Never the executor of the same run (V3-D5).

then.description: A VERIFY cannot return CHANGES_REQUIRED (contract §5): there is no second repair for it to request. It reports a standing blocker as UNRESOLVED_BLOCKER instead, which is the value round PROMISE-PATH-VOCAB added so that outcome stops borrowing SPEC_GAP's name.

A FULL has no accepted-finding scope to declare — it is the round that produces the findings. Its verdict narrowing is stated here rather than left to the root enum: since the root grew to the union of both rounds, a root-only constraint would let a FULL return the VERIFY-only UNRESOLVED_BLOCKER, and contract §5's FULL row is closed at three.
CHANGES_REQUIRED with no findings would demand a change without naming one.

UNRESOLVED_BLOCKER with no findings would report a blocker without naming it, and the run stops on this verdict — the sibling of the CHANGES_REQUIRED rule above, and the reason the flow can enumerate what stands. That at least one of those findings is blocking is check_review_result_v2's, which has the findings and this schema's enum in one place.

evidence_commit.description: The exact commit that carries the run's committed control plane — the whole review subject, as one SHA. The reviewer re-derives every member from this commit and the revisions the WorkSpec and CandidateRecord pin; nothing is taken from executor-supplied bytes. The only field of this binding that does not already exist in the CandidateRecord.

candidate_ref.description: The exact payload candidate reviewed. The commit is required even though candidateRef leaves it optional: a review bound to a branch name alone would follow the branch as it moves — the 'review candidate A, accept candidate B' failure class (V3-D5).

control_root.description: The run's control root E(C). The evidence commit's changed-path set must lie inside it (supersession-1 S2; checked by check_subject, never hoped).

repair_round.description: 0 = the original candidate C reviewed by FULL; 1 = C2, the single user-approved repair, reviewed by VERIFY (V3-D6). Cross-checked against the CandidateRecord read from the evidence commit.

reviewSubject.description: The commit-bound review subject. Every field is cross-checked by the v2-aware result checker against the CandidateRecord AT the evidence commit — a result naming a different candidate, round, base, root, work or run than the committed control plane records is rejected (W2-A9), which is the 'check candidate A, report candidate B' class (V3-D5) closed at the result layer without a package object.
